headline: Bohm's 10th-inning sac fly walks off Nationals
recap: The Phillies beat the Washington Nationals 6-5 in 10 innings at Citizens Bank Park, breaking a 5-5 tie in the bottom of the 10th. J.T. Realmuto, who began the inning on second base under that season's extra-inning rule, advanced to third on a Didi Gregorius sacrifice bunt. Nationals reliever Sean Doolittle then intentionally walked Jean Segura and Phil Gosselin to load the bases before Alec Bohm's sacrifice fly to center field brought Realmuto home for the win.

Zach Eflin started for Philadelphia and allowed four runs on seven hits over six innings with five strikeouts; Aníbal Sánchez started for Washington and worked three and one-third innings. Trea Turner tied the game at 2-2 in the third with an inside-the-park home run to right-center and finished 3-for-5 with three RBI, adding a run-scoring groundout in the fifth that made it 4-4.

Gregorius drove in three runs, an RBI single that put the Phillies up 2-0 in the first and an RBI double in the third, when Rhys Hoskins also homered to make it 4-2. Andrew McCutchen's forceout in the eighth scored Gregorius to tie it 5-5. Héctor Neris worked a scoreless ninth, and Blake Parker (3-0) picked up the win after pitching around two walks in the top of the 10th; Doolittle (0-2) took the loss.
